popCulture.title: Amphictyon
popCulture.description: Son of Deucalion (or of the soil), early king of Attica who succeeds Cranaus — host of Dionysus and namesake of the Amphictyonic leagues in later aetiology.

popCulture.title: Dionysus
popCulture.description: Pausanias and Apollodorus remember Amphictyon as the Attic king who first entertained Dionysus and mixed wine with water — hospitality rewritten as a civic first.

popCulture.title: Deucalion
popCulture.description: In one strand Amphictyon's father — the flood-survivor whose son's Attic reign bridges the Deucalionic age and Cecrops' line.

popCulture.title: Amphictyonic League
popCulture.description: Later Greeks derived the Delphic and other amphictyonies from this king's name — mythic eponym for sacred interstate councils.
